stem: Across PIE's within- and cross-dataset settings, by what factor did its AUPRC for differentially expressed genes exceed the strongest baseline in each setting?
label: Abstract · headline AUPRC gain

stem: Why does PIE predict population-level effects for each condition rather than the expression state of individual perturbed cells?
choices: It lets the model reuse pretrained single-cell foundation model weights
It removes the need for unperturbed control cells at test time
It gives a more direct training signal and aids transfer to new conditions
It allows training on bulk RNA-seq instead of single-cell data
answer: It gives a more direct training signal and aids transfer to new conditions
label: Design · population-level target

stem: What lets PIE predict perturbation outcomes for genes it never saw during training?
choices: A shared gene vocabulary is harmonized across all training datasets
Missing genes are imputed from co-expressed neighbours in a gene network
Per-gene learned embeddings are transferred by sequence homology
Each output gene is encoded from its text description plus measured evidence
answer: Each output gene is encoded from its text description plus measured evidence
label: Design · no fixed gene vocabulary

stem: During training, why does PIE randomly zero out its Same-pert and Same-context Evidence for a subset of samples?
choices: So it can still predict when a channel is missing, as for new entities
To regularize against overfitting to highly expressed genes
To balance class weights between DE and non-DE genes
To simulate the dropout noise typical of single-cell data
answer: So it can still predict when a channel is missing, as for new entities
label: Design · evidence dropout

stem: Which four cell lines make up the Replogle–Nadig CRISPRi benchmark used as PIE's main dataset?
label: Setup · benchmark cell lines

stem: In the experiment holding out the whole Replogle–Nadig dataset, what was removed from training so that its contexts were also new?
choices: Every perturbation measured in the held-out dataset
Every CRISPRi dataset, leaving only small-molecule data
Every shared cell line, including lines derived from them
Every gene outside the held-out dataset's panel
answer: Every shared cell line, including lines derived from them
label: Setup · cross-dataset exclusion

stem: For unseen cell-line contexts within Replogle–Nadig, what DE AUPRC did PIE reach versus Rhaister-O?

choices: Spearman correlation of log fold changes
label: Within-dataset · the one exception

stem: For unseen perturbations in seen contexts, how did PIE's DE AUPRC compare with the strongest baseline, TabICL?
label: Within-dataset · unseen perturbations

stem: With both context and perturbation unseen within Replogle–Nadig, which model was the only applicable comparator for PIE?
label: Within-dataset · both unseen

stem: With both context and perturbation unseen, what Discrimination Score L1 did PIE reach versus the context-mean baseline?
label: Within-dataset · discrimination

stem: Besides Replogle–Nadig, on which datasets did PIE significantly outperform the strongest baseline in within-dataset experiments?
choices: Jiang et al. and Arc VCC 2025
label: Within-dataset · other datasets

stem: Transferring to the held-out Replogle–Nadig dataset, what DE AUPRC did PIE achieve for perturbations seen in training, versus Rhaister-O?
label: Cross-dataset · seen perturbations

stem: In transfer to Replogle–Nadig with seen perturbations, which baseline edged out PIE, and on which metric?
choices: Perturbation mean, on DE direction match
answer: Perturbation mean, on DE direction match
label: Cross-dataset · the one exception

stem: In transfer to Replogle–Nadig with seen perturbations, what Spearman effect-size correlation did PIE reach versus Rhaister-O?
label: Cross-dataset · effect size

stem: Transferring to Replogle–Nadig for perturbations absent from every training dataset, what DE AUPRC did PIE achieve versus context mean?
label: Cross-dataset · unseen perturbations

stem: When Jiang et al., X-Atlas/Orion or Arc VCC 2025 was the held-out dataset instead, how did PIE's DE AUPRC rank?
choices: Highest for seen but below Rhaister-O for unseen perturbations
Highest for both seen and unseen perturbations
Below perturbation mean for both perturbation regimes
Highest only when Arc VCC 2025 was held out
answer: Highest for both seen and unseen perturbations
label: Cross-dataset · other held-out datasets

stem: In the Shapley ablation for unseen contexts, which two input groups explained most of the AUPRC rise from 0.238 to 0.422?
choices: Control Mean Evidence and Context Description
Same-pert Evidence and Perturbation Knowledge Sources
Control Mean Evidence and Same-context Evidence
answer: Same-pert Evidence and Perturbation Knowledge Sources
label: Ablation · unseen contexts

stem: In the Shapley ablation for unseen perturbations, how large was the AUPRC gain from all input groups and how was it distributed?
choices: A large gain of 0.184, mostly from Same-pert Evidence
A small gain of 0.045, mostly from Control Mean Evidence
A gain of 0.010, entirely from knowledge sources
A small gain of 0.045, spread across all five groups
answer: A small gain of 0.045, spread across all five groups
label: Ablation · unseen perturbations

stem: For unseen perturbations, which input group accounted for nearly all of the gain in Discrimination Score L1?
label: Ablation · discrimination driver

stem: With both context and perturbation unseen, how did Perturbation Knowledge Sources contribute in the Shapley ablation?
choices: Drove most of the AUPRC gain but hurt direction match and LFC correlation
Hurt AUPRC on average but drove most direction, LFC and discrimination gains
Helped every metric, with their largest gain on DE AUPRC ranking
Helped only Discrimination Score L1, leaving other metrics unchanged
answer: Hurt AUPRC on average but drove most direction, LFC and discrimination gains
label: Ablation · both unseen

stem: In the per-source ablation for unseen perturbations, which Perturbation Knowledge Source contributed the most AUPRC?
label: Ablation · per-source AUPRC

stem: Which Perturbation Knowledge Source had a negative AUPRC Shapley value in all three within-dataset regimes?
choices: The ESM2 protein embedding of the target
The STRING network embedding of the target
The DepMap viability profile of the target
The NCBI text description of the target
answer: The NCBI text description of the target
label: Ablation · negative source

stem: Which three measured activity profiles does PIE use to describe a chemical perturbation?
choices: L1000 transcription, PRISM viability and JUMP morphology
L1000 transcription, DepMap viability and STRING interactions
PRISM viability, ESM2 embeddings and JUMP morphology
DepMap viability, L1000 transcription and Cellosaurus text
answer: L1000 transcription, PRISM viability and JUMP morphology
label: Inputs · chemical knowledge sources

stem: How does PIE define the binary differential-expression label for a gene in a condition?
choices: Welch t-test with Bonferroni-adjusted p below 0.05
Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR below 0.05
Absolute log2 fold change above 1 versus control cells
Wilcoxon rank-sum test with unadjusted p below 0.01
answer: Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR below 0.05
label: Setup · DE label

choices: Small molecules at the highest dose
label: Limitation · small effects

stem: In which generalization setting did the authors say PIE's performance declined?
choices: Seen perturbations in an unseen dataset
Unseen genetic perturbations in seen contexts
